overview: This bill, the Chief Herbert D. Proffitt Act of 2025, expands the Public Safety Officers' Benefits program, which pays benefits when police officers, firefighters and other first responders are killed or permanently disabled in the line of duty. Under the bill, retired law enforcement officers who left in good standing would also qualify if they are killed or permanently and totally disabled in a targeted attack because of their past police service. The change would apply to such attacks that happened on or after January 1, 2012, and to claims already pending. The Senate passed it on July 29, 2025, and the House received it on August 1, 2025.
for: Supporters say officers can be targeted for revenge long after they retire, and their families deserve the same support as those of officers harmed while on duty.
against: Critics say extending benefits to retirees and reaching back to attacks since 2012 adds cost to the program and could make it harder to determine whether an attack was truly tied to an officer's past service.
